newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Mawhinney seeks to calm Euro currency row.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Mawhinney seeks to calm Euro currency row.

text.p: The chairman of Britain's ruling Conservative Party on Saturday tried to smooth over an apparent rift in government policy on a single European currency, insisting ministers were united on the issue.

Brian Mawhinney was speaking at the end of a week in which Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind said the government was "on balance hostile" to the planned single currency, a remark interpreted by some as indicating a new emphasis in policy.
Mawhinney said policy had not changed and in any case the planned Euro currency was unlikely to come into being on schedule in 1999.
"You know the policy hasn't changed. You know we are doubtful about whether a single currency will even proceed in 1999," he told an interviewer on BBC radio.
Mawhinney dismissed suggestions that the cabinet was split on the issue of the single currency.
"I'm supportive of the same policy as all of the members of the cabinet. We are all supportive of the same policy," he said.
Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke earlier this week dismissed Rifkind's remark as a slip of the tongue and both men said policy was unchanged.
